reviewer: Independent separate agent; same GPT family, cross-family requirement NOT_SATISFIED
scope: Pinned cached README/license text for nine added archive candidates; six extra BlazeDiff upstream/license texts. No code installed or executed, no API/model inference, no runtime certification.

corrections.text: Add Node.js for validators and an OS-enforced sandbox with sanitized environment, networking disabled and resource/write limits before executing any target-controlled tests. Tool-using subagents alone do not provide that boundary.

Keep REUSE explicitly limited to reviewed methodology/ledger/schema as already described in the acceptance criterion; it is not approval to install/execute the skill or a completed security certification.
Separate local d3k requirements from the remote/sandbox launcher, which the README limits to macOS, with Vercel login/access and additional tools. Do not imply Windows supports the sandbox mode.

The source has inconsistent budget descriptions: an earlier fx section says a non-renewing $5 session cap, while the newer Eve default section says no session spending cap. Budget default must remain UNKNOWN/harness-dependent until source-code/configuration review and a bounded test; do not claim a safe cap from this README.

The live timeline is bounded to 5,000 events/8 MiB and disappears on exit; body/redaction capture is selective and best effort. Add evidence-gap/eviction handling and an explicitly authorized durable evidence export rather than treating d3k as a durable audit ledger.

Use: MIT for inspected BlazeDiff code; embedded MILO weights are Apache-2.0; original reference-code terms and notices are separately described. Algorithm/dependency/commercial-rights clearance remains NOT_AUDITED. The reference MATLAB SSIM/MS-SSIM restrictions must not be blindly applied to the independently MIT-claimed implementation, or ignored for imported reference code.

Distinguish deterministic core/metric calculations from the optional agent-in-the-loop product. Vendor speed/parity claims and learned perceptual metrics are not independently tested or UX acceptance.

Retain the explicit whole-running-Chrome/logged-in-user boundary and DEFER decision. The current README says Browser Harness is the engine inside Browser Use; installing both is not an independent engine comparison. Its benchmark used a shared fresh cloud browser, not each tool's default local session.

Replace ambiguous URL/ZIP traversal wording with: untrusted file paths, remote URLs and archive contents require validation and resource limits; no specific path-traversal vulnerability was demonstrated. The README expressly states current-process I/O privileges, broad convert(), and narrower convert_local/convert_stream APIs. Narrow APIs are not a sandbox by themselves.

Python 3.10-3.14 is supported by README. Preserve selective extras/plugins-off-by-default and local-only dependencies; image captioning/transcription and Azure conversion paths are remote/billable options.

Authentication configuration alone does not close the README's default-open Ollama-compatible /api/* routes. Include the documented whitelist restriction and verify unauthenticated access is denied across every exposed route. The host=0.0.0.0/auth-off statement is a pinned README observation, not a current AWE runtime finding.

Default KV/vector/graph/doc-status backends are in-memory with local file persistence and are described as evaluation-only, not production. Storage/model/embedding configuration and reindex/delete behavior need separate acceptance.

README now lists Windows as well as Linux/macOS/mobile and OS-specific SDK features; do not preserve a Linux-only assumption. It specifies 64-bit Python 3.10-3.14. Writes are single-process exclusive although multiple processes may read.

WAL durability/performance claims are source assertions to test, not evidence of PostgreSQL transaction/RLS/auth equivalence. Keep the crash/reopen, isolation and measured-advantage pilot rather than replacing current storage.

Local SDK/index storage does not imply offline inference: source examples still use an LLM API key. Cloud mode also transfers indexing/storage to the vendor; make dataflow, model cost and cloud storage explicit. Subscription-based Claude invocation remains an advertised integration, not an independent grant of provider permission or guaranteed quota.
Keep source benchmark/indexing-cost headlines separate from AWE measurements and from cloud/subscription pricing. No quoted savings/cost/accuracy figure has been reproduced in this audit.

Explicitly reject/filter extractions whose char_interval is None. The README acknowledges hallucinated extraction from few-shot examples; a valid schema or source-looking text is insufficient. Also test wrong/overlapping spans and factual attributes that go beyond source text.

Do not promise identical schema enforcement across providers: the README says Ollama does not currently support output_schema. Google organization ownership does not mean an officially supported Google product; the disclaimer says otherwise.

framing: 50 source-linked desk reviews are not 50 runtime or security audits.
